title: New World $25 Million Offer From Rust Dev Was A Joke But Studio Has Talked With Amazon
description: After Amazon announced that its MMO New World would close down in January 2027, Alistair McFarlane--the director and COO at Rust studio Facepunch--made an "offer" of $25 million to buy the game. He has now confirmed this was a joke, but followed up to say he has actually spoken to current and former Amazon staff, adding that the team at Facepunch is "always looking at new opportunities." "What started off as a joke between a colleague and me on X quickly took on a life of its own. I genuinely appreciate everyone who's reached out over the last few days, including current and former Amazon Games staff who have offered their support and insight," he wrote. McFarlane added that he and others at Facepunch have "a ton of love" for New World, adding that the game "didn't receive the long-term support it could and should have." Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: WoW Mods Are Changing Forever Today
description: World of Warcraft: Midnight's expansion pre-patch is out later today on January 20, and once it's live, many of the game's player-made mods for assisting in combat (add-ons) will look and function much differently than before. In some cases, they may not even work at all. Announced early last year, Blizzard is finally ripping off the combat add-on Band-Aid today in an effort to make WoW more understandable out of the box and make it so add-ons don't offer distinct advantages in combat. For well over a decade, players doing endgame raids or high-level Mythic+ dungeons have always relied on combat add-ons to make the game easier to parse. Sometimes that meant specific boss callouts or solutions for certain boss mechanics. Other times it meant custom reminders on when to use specific abilities. That's changing come pre-patch. Many of the add-ons that have over the years essentially become required for playing WoW competently, like the damage meter Details! and encounter-helper add-on Deadly Boss Mods, will instead be baked into WoW's own default user interface. It should, in theory, raise the floor for all WoW players, who now will all have a baseline UI to work from that offers much of the important information add-ons used to provide. Combined with Blizzard's encounter design efforts to make it so add-ons aren't required in order to succeed, WoW's endgame will likely feel much different than in years past. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Developer's Office Rocked By An Explosion
description: Rockstar North, the development studio behind Grand Theft Auto 6, was struck by an explosion earlier this week at its office in Edinburgh, Scotland. The explosion occurred at 5:02 AM local time on January 19, and it apparently took place in the facility's boiler room. According to BNO News, the incident set off a small fire at Rockstar North's office, and emergency response crews were on the scene for four hours. No injuries were reported from the fire or explosion, and Rockstar issued a statement that thanked the first responders and assured fans that GTA 6 development wasn't affected. "Many thanks to those that reached out with concern, and also to the police and fire crews who were on scene quickly to access the situation. Please know that everyone is well and our studio remains open and operational." Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Life Is Strange: Reunion Finally Brings Back Chloe Price
description: Deck Nine and Square Enix have officially revealed Life is Strange: Reunion after a tease last week and an Xbox Wire leak earlier today. It's out in March and is meant to serve as the culmination and conclusion of Max Caulfield and Chloe Price's story. Yes, Chloe Price is returning in Life is Strange: Reunion after not appearing in 2024's Double Exposure, to the chagrin of the series' fan base. It'll follow the pair as they reunite following Max's merging of realities at the end of Double Exposure and Chloe's time either being dead or serving as a tour manager for a band called Drugstore Makeup. A fire is seemingly destined to destroy Caledon University, where Max has settled down. The key to preventing that (and some more cataclysmic events in the future) will force Max and Chloe to reunite and work together. The stream featuring the game's announcement trailer revealed more, like the fact that it will account for whether or not players decided to let Chloe die at the end of the original. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: What To Do First In Hytale
description: Hytale is out now in early access, and when you first spawn into a fresh world, you'll notice a few things. For starters, if you've ever seen or played Minecraft before, you'll feel like you're in a familiar place, as Hytale looks extremely similar. Not only that, but Hytale also follows an almost identical gameplay loop to Minecraft. You spawn into a randomly-generated map and must scavenge for resources around you to create equipment, a base, and advance your character. While Minecraft veterans might feel right at home with this sort of gameplay, other players could use a sense of direction. There are no quest markers, few NPCs to meet, or objects to point you towards a specific location. You can always figure things out for yourself, but if you need some guidance, check out the guide below that gives you some ideas on what to do first in Hytale. title: Marathon Might Be Part Of A Dying Breed Of Game, Former Art Director Says
description: Bungie's upcoming anticipated extraction shooter, Marathon, is scheduled to arrive in early March, and is, as of this writing, one of the highest-selling games over on Steam. Even with the alleged stolen-art controversy, it's looking like Marathon could be the winner that Bungie needs it to be after Concord failed to take off. According to former art director Joseph Cross, that level of commitment to an unproven IP might be a thing of the past soon. In an interview with ReaderGrev, Cross feels like the state of funding for games has reached a point where studios shouldn't blindly fund games based on spec and compares Concord to Marathon on the same sort of production scale. "Marathon is such a massive project. The studio took such a risk on this. You know, oftentimes we felt like we were sort of getting away with something," he said. "I think about that in the big picture, the idea of studios funding unproven, unknown projects for six or eight years, for hundreds of millions of dollars, sort of on spec. How much longer are things like this going to exist? I've been part of a couple of them now." Continue Reading at GameSpot
